alt: An Apple iPhone Duo foldable phone open to show its flexible inner display and distinctive book-fold hinge — the same hinge mechanism later found to press against the display electronics, cracking screens in reported units
story: Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo ($1,999), launched October 23, 2026; within weeks owners reported a crunching hinge sound followed by a horizontal row of dead pixels on the inner screen — iFixit's teardown found the hinge's center support bar doesn't retract far enough and presses directly into the display electronics; Apple acknowledged the issue and explained its hinge assembly used 'AI algorithms' to match components, with replacement screens costing $999 out of warranty.
why_funny: Apple advertised the iPhone Duo as achieving 'a visually crease-free state' and shipped a $2,000 phone whose hinge cracks its own screen — then explained the hinge design process involved AI, as if that made it less broken.
